$comment: Generic example: User Authentication System analysis

components.description: Core authentication service handling user login, logout, and credential validation. Coordinates with SessionManager and PasswordValidator to manage authentication lifecycle.
components.business_purpose: Ensures secure user access to the system by validating credentials against stored user data and enforcing password policies.

key_methods.description: Validates user credentials and creates session on success
Terminates user session and invalidates session token
Checks if session token is valid and not expired

components.notes: Well-structured component with clear separation of concerns. Password hashing uses BCrypt algorithm.

components.description: Manages user session lifecycle including token generation, validation, timeout handling, and session cleanup.
components.business_purpose: Maintains stateful user sessions to track authenticated users and enforce session expiration policies for security.

key_methods.description: Generates new session token and stores in session cache
Removes session from active sessions and marks token as invalid
Extends session timeout if within renewal window

components.notes: Uses Redis for distributed session management. Session timeout configured at 30 minutes with 5-minute renewal window.

components.description: Validates password complexity requirements and handles password hashing/verification using BCrypt algorithm.
components.business_purpose: Enforces password security policies to protect user accounts from unauthorized access and brute-force attacks.

key_methods.description: Checks password meets minimum length, complexity requirements
Creates BCrypt hash of password with salt
Verifies plain password matches stored hash

components.notes: Password policy: minimum 8 characters, requires uppercase, lowercase, digit, and special character. Uses BCrypt with cost factor 12.

business_rules.description: After 5 consecutive failed login attempts, user account is locked for 15 minutes
business_rules.pseudocode:
IF failed_attempts >= 5 THEN
  SET account_locked = true
  SET lockout_until = current_time + 15 minutes
  RETURN 'Account locked'
END IF
business_rules.business_impact: Prevents brute-force password attacks while allowing legitimate users to regain access after timeout
business_rules.notes: Lockout counter resets on successful login. Admin can manually unlock accounts.

business_rules.description: User sessions expire after 30 minutes of inactivity. Sessions can be renewed within 5-minute window before expiration.
business_rules.pseudocode:
IF (current_time - last_activity) > 30 minutes THEN
  INVALIDATE session
  RETURN 'Session expired'
ELSE IF (current_time - last_activity) > 25 minutes THEN
  ALLOW renewal
END IF
business_rules.business_impact: Balances security (limiting exposure of idle sessions) with user experience (preventing frequent re-authentication)
business_rules.notes: Session activity updated on each authenticated API request

business_rules.description: Passwords must be minimum 8 characters with at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one digit, and one special character
business_rules.pseudocode:
IF length < 8 THEN REJECT
IF NOT contains_uppercase THEN REJECT
IF NOT contains_lowercase THEN REJECT
IF NOT contains_digit THEN REJECT
IF NOT contains_special_char THEN REJECT
RETURN 'Valid'
business_rules.business_impact: Ensures password strength to protect user accounts from dictionary attacks and common password vulnerabilities

data_flows.description: Complete authentication flow from credential submission to session creation
steps: User submits username and password via login form
UserRepository queries database for user record
data_flows.security_considerations: Password transmitted over HTTPS only. Password hash never returned to client. Session token includes CSRF protection.

data_flows.description: Validates session token for authenticated API requests
steps: Client includes session token in API request header
Check if session exists and not expired (AUTH-BR-002)
Return user context for request processing
data_flows.security_considerations: Session tokens are UUID v4. Token validation occurs before any business logic execution.

external_dependencies.description: PostgreSQL database storing user credentials and profile data
Redis cache for distributed session storage
Centralized audit logging service for authentication events
external_dependencies.integration_point: Log4j integration for login attempts, logouts, lockouts
external_dependencies.notes: Audit logs include timestamp, username, IP address, success/failure status

technical_debt.description: Password reset functionality not implemented - currently requires admin intervention
technical_debt.migration_impact: Should be included in modern microservices implementation
Recommended for enhanced security in VNRM equivalent

technical_debt.description: Session storage lacks backup/persistence - Redis failure causes all sessions to be lost
technical_debt.migration_impact: Implement Redis persistence or session database backup

migration_notes.recommended_target_architecture: Separate Authentication Service (OAuth2/JWT) with centralized Session Management
modernization_opportunities: Replace custom session tokens with JWT for stateless authentication
Implement OAuth2/OpenID Connect for third-party authentication
Implement passwordless authentication options (biometric, magic links)
Add rate limiting at API gateway level to complement lockout mechanism
